scope: Bounded review of effective ISO 32000-2:2020 EC3 §§8.3.1, 8.3.2.1, .2, .4, and .5. Excludes detailed re-review of §8.3.2.3 user space, §8.3.3/.4 matrix arithmetic, page geometry, and graphics-state stack already treated in coordinates_graphics_state_current; cross-references those findings where needed. This is feature-level evidence, not whole-§8.3 certification.
source_method: Held primary PDF doc/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf, text and footer checked with pdftotext -layout. Physical pages 164–167 correspond to printed 149–152. The annotations on these pages are /Link navigation targets; no coordinate-specific errata annotation was found. EC3 does not change the listed coordinate-foundation text in the checked inventory.

features.title: General
source_features: Introduces coordinate systems as defining position, orientation, and size of two-dimensional text, graphics, and images on the page.
NOTE points 3D artwork to §13.6.5; it is explanatory scope, not a separate 2D mapping algorithm.
features.ledger: Clause inventory says implemented; this row is too general to prove the constituent mapping rules by itself.
features.implementation: The content interpreter turns page content into display-list marks with explicit transforms; pdf-render maps those to a requested raster target. Unsupported drawing is reported through Interpretation rather than silently claimed complete.
features.assertions: No isolated assertion for the general description. The public page/raster tests cited under §§8.3.2.1/.2 and the previous coordinates_graphics_state_current shard exercise the constituent behavior. 3D annotation/artwork behavior was not tested in this shard.
features.verdict: No distinct defect indicated by the general paragraph. Do not treat a general row's implemented label as proof of all coordinate-space relationships.
residuals: 3D coordinate projection in §13.6.5 is outside this bounded review; no support or non-support claim is made here.

features.title: General
source_features: Paths and positions shall use Cartesian x/y coordinate pairs of real numbers.
A coordinate space is characterized relative to the current page by origin, x/y orientation, and unit lengths.
Transformations between spaces are represented by transformation matrices; examples named include translation, scale, rotation, reflection, and skew.
features.ledger: Implemented at aggregate level; no ledger-specific numerical precision/tolerance promise is recorded for these general statements.
features.implementation: PDF numeric operands are read as f64 and narrowed to the renderer's f32 Point/Transform representation; affine maps and raster target transforms carry the origin, axes, and scale. The renderer's internal precision is an implementation representation, not a source-defined coordinate grid.
features.assertions: Existing exact-transform/content tests use integer values and noncommuting matrices; page geometry has a fractional MediaBox example, and text-positioning tests assert fractional advances. Those are positive evidence for real-valued inputs but do not characterize precision at very large or near-pixel-boundary coordinates.
features.verdict: No demonstrated error. The standard says real numbers but supplies no error tolerance for raster realization or mandate for f64 internal storage; f32 rounding is a precision-policy residual, not by itself a conformance failure.
residuals: No independent end-to-end fractional content-coordinate oracle was added; extreme-coordinate precision and tiny-scale representation remain outside this review.

features.title: Device space
source_features: Device coordinates, origin, axis orientation, and resolution vary by output device; the text uses raster display and printer examples.
NOTE explains that specifying page objects directly in device space would make the document device-dependent.
features.ledger: Implemented at aggregate level; the clause describes device variation rather than requiring one device transform.
features.implementation: pdf-render::TargetSpec supplies the output scale and pixel bounds; the CPU backend rasterizes display-list coordinates into that target. The PDF page transform remains device-independent and device scaling is applied at output.
features.assertions: page_geometry.rs checks that default user-space units map at requested raster scale and that UserUnit changes physical dimensions; image/page tests sample the resulting output. No test attempts to standardize a device origin or pixel resolution, which the source explicitly leaves device-dependent.
features.verdict: No gap identified in the reader obligation at this layer. Do not infer that the PDF file itself must choose a fixed device-space origin/resolution.
residuals: Specific printer/display coordinate origins and anisotropic device resolutions are not modeled as distinct physical devices; that is a renderer-target/host concern and no ISO default is stated here.

features.title: Other coordinate spaces
source_features: Text space maps to user space through text matrix and text-state parameters.
Glyph space maps to text space through a font matrix; most font types use their predefined 1000-unit mapping, while Type 3 supplies FontMatrix.
Image space is a fixed one-by-one unit square independent of sample dimensions, mapped to user space by temporarily changing CTM.
Form and pattern spaces map through their own matrices.
3D artwork has 3D coordinates projected into an annotation target coordinate system.
features.ledger: Aggregate implemented row overlaps many narrowly assigned children; it is not an independent proof that each special-space mapping is correct.
features.implementation: Specialized consumers compose text matrices/font matrices, Type 3 FontMatrix, image unit-square transforms, Form XObject Matrix, and tiling-pattern Matrix into the active transform. Relevant paths include content/text, content/text/type3.rs, content/image, content/xobject.rs, and content/pattern.rs.
features.assertions: Independent checks exist in text_positioning_audit.rs, type3_spec_audit.rs, image_coordinates_audit.rs (3x2 image mapped to 60x60 unit-space area, with literal source-color cells and skew/reflection), form_xobjects_audit.rs, and tiling.rs. These tests exercise different coordinate-space consumers rather than a single general mapping oracle. 3D projection remains unreviewed here.
features.verdict: The listed 2D space mappings have direct consumer-level evidence in their specialized shards. No new test is justified here; avoid treating those samples as full coverage of every font, image, form, or pattern transformation.
residuals: No claim on §13.6.5's 3D projection or support policy.
Some linked evidence belongs to specialized audits and is not re-certified by this bounded foundation review.

features.title: Relationships among coordinate spaces
source_features: Figure 12 is a relationship diagram: arrows denote transformations between named coordinate spaces.

The prose says coordinate spaces are defined relative to one another and changing a transformation can affect objects in several spaces; example: user-to-device CTM affects forms, text, images, and patterns upstream of user space.
features.ledger: Implemented at aggregate level. The figure and example synthesize child-space transforms; they do not add a separate matrix operator or independent required rendering algorithm.
features.implementation: Display-list commands carry composed transforms; page CTM enters interpreter state and nested text/image/form/pattern calls concatenate their respective transforms before producing marks.
features.assertions: The composed noncommuting cm + page CropBox/Rotate/UserUnit test in coordinate_graphics_state_current checks full page mapping and q/Q restoration. Image, form, text, and pattern tests listed above assert their specialized mapping effects. The previous coordinate shard records the matrix-order control; this artifact does not duplicate it.
features.verdict: No independent defect found in the relationships prose/diagram. Evidence is distributed across consumers, and the broad clause-level implemented status remains a coarse ledger label.
residuals: No single regression composes every listed special coordinate space; this is not required to restate their separate transformation rules and would add little beyond specialized controls.
